title: Germany: IG Metall union says deal reached with employers
summary: IG Metall, representing millions of workers in Germany's metal and electrical industry, is the country's largest trade union. The deal came after more than 24 hours of talks with employers.

image.caption: IG Metall was founded in 1949Image: Julian Stratenschulte/dpa/picture alliance

blocks.text: Germany's powerful IG Metall trade union said Thursday it has reached a pay deal with employers after more than 24 hours of talks.
IG Metall and employers agreed on the following points in their agreement:

items: The deal foresees a pay increase in two phases: 2.0% from May 2027 and 2.3% from April 2028
The agreement will also entail one-off payments in March 2027 of between €150 ($164) and €450

blocks.text: What is IG Metal and what are the significance of the talks?
IG Metall represents 3.7 million workers in the German metal and electrical industry. It is Germany's largest trade union.
The talks come amid job cuts across multiple sectors in the German economy, such as the automotive sector.
IG Metall represents workers in major German companies such as Volkswagen, Mercedes-Benz, Siemens, ThyssenKrupp, and Salzgitter AG, among others.
